newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Haggie sees better full year results.
newsitem.headline: Haggie sees better full year results.

text.p: Haggie Ltd said on Wednesday it expected its full year results to show a significant improvement over those of calendar 1996.

"Competitive conditions are likely to result in (second half) financial results being a little weaker than the first half, but still better than the previous year," Haggie's Chairman Tony Harris said in a statement.
The company earlier announced its headline earnings per share for the six months to June 30, up at 131 cents compared with 129 cents in the previous corresponding half year.
Haggie's headline earnings for the full 1996 were 199 cents, 41 percent lower than the previous year.
The group said strong international competition, both in local and world markets, and low margins had pared its operating profitability over the first half.
Operating profits rose six percent to 48.6 million rand.
Harris said Haggie's first half debt to equity ratio had improved to 19 percent from 24 percent at the end of 1996 with a further reduction expected by the end of the year.
Better volumes were seen narrowing full year losses at the group's Steel Cord unit, he added.
Haggie manufactures a broad range of steel, rope and wire products, including tools, for the engineering industry.
